findings.title: Happy-path verified-move coverage claim is inaccurate
findings.action: No action needed — refuted; the verified-move happy path is already covered by "CLI carry-check: verified directory move → exit 0, one JSON line" and by multiple cases in test/spec-refresh-carry.test.mjs (e.g. "verified directory move carries (reason paths-only)").
findings.disposition_rationale: The finding claims the only positive-path assertion in the diff is a trivial pathExists('docs/x.md')===true unit test. That is false: test/spec-review-carry-check.test.mjs already has a dedicated CLI-level test exercising the exact verified-move happy path end to end, and test/spec-refresh-carry.test.mjs has several more at the classifier level.

findings.title: Symlinked carry-check root not explicitly exercised by a genuine-move test
findings.action: Added a dedicated test proving a genuine move under a root reached through a symlink still resolves true, closing the coverage gap.
findings.disposition_rationale: makePathExists already realpaths both root and the candidate before comparing (plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/spec-review.js), so a symlinked-root happy path already worked; the finding's real, actionable kernel was the missing explicit test, which commit e32f5936 added.

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/spec-review.js::toctou between the two existence probes in carry-check
findings.title: TOCTOU between the two existence probes in carry-check
findings.action: Accepted as a documented, fail-safe-direction limitation; no code change.
findings.disposition_rationale: The finding itself states the direction is fail-safe: a filesystem change between the two existence probes can only flip a verified move to unverified (re-review), never the reverse. A one-shot CLI classifying prep-authored spec files is not a target worth adding locking/retry machinery for; the risk is accepted.

occurrences.title: TOCTOU between the two existence probes in carry-check

findings.finding_id: test/spec-review-carry-check.test.mjs::windows portability of the symlink-based containment tests
findings.title: Windows portability of the symlink-based containment tests
findings.action: Accepted; consistent with the existing codebase-wide convention of unguarded symlinkSync in tests, out of scope for this change.
findings.disposition_rationale: Over ten other existing test files in this repo already use fs.symlinkSync with no win32 guard (e.g. test/doctor.test.mjs, test/resume-store.test.mjs, test/bundle.test.mjs). Singling out this PR's three new symlink tests for Windows-specific handling would be inconsistent with the rest of the suite and is a separate, repo-wide concern.

occurrences.title: Windows portability of the symlink-based containment tests

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/spec-refresh-carry.js::path-move-unverified reason string conflates "both exist" with an unverified move
findings.title: path-move-unverified reason string conflates "both exist" with an unverified move
findings.action: Accepted as a cosmetic naming nit; the exit code and fail-safe direction are correct, so the reason string is left unchanged.
findings.disposition_rationale: The finding itself calls this harmless. Both the both-exist and neither-exists cases are genuinely "not a verified move", which is exactly what the reason name states; a consumer reading path_moves[].verified already gets the precise signal.

findings.title: pathExists('.') test pins an implementation detail (rel === "")
findings.action: Accepted; left as-is given the low risk and the test's own inline comment already explaining the invariant it checks.
findings.disposition_rationale: The asserted behaviour (root itself is never a valid move target) is the actual spec-level property path-move-unverified-ness depends on; the test's comment already documents why, so the coupling to the internal rel==="" shape is intentional and low-cost to fix forward if the resolver ever changes.
